notes: UK-domiciled (Cayman parent, English operating sub Arqit Limited) quantum encryption company. Filing names UK Government, European Space Agency, BT, Sumitomo as customers, with Verizon, BP, NEOM, Juniper, Dentons, Northrup [sic] Grumman, Iridium as testers. No specific U.S. DoD Program Element numbers (PE numbers) are named in the filing. Closest DoD-program proximity is (a) NATO-allied government framing of the Federated Quantum System (FQS), and (b) board members with prior USAF / DoD-JROC roles. Pentagon J-Book corpus coverage is therefore expected to be low — most queries will return NOT_FOUND/UNVERIFIABLE rather than UNFUNDED. Control claims included for patents/facilities/counterparty disclosure.

claims.claim_text: ARQQ has a $1 billion sales pipeline of customer contracts in various stages of negotiation and initial revenue indications from potential customers (i.e., not yet contractually committed).
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.source_quote: Arqit's backlog estimates consisted of approximately $130 million in customer contracts, and Arqit had an estimated $1[.07?] billion in pipeline, consisting of customer contracts in various stages of negotiation and initial revenue indications from potential customers that have not been contractually committed.

claims.claim_text: ARQQ has $130 million of backlog from signed customer contracts as of September 30, 2021, supporting forward revenue.
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.source_quote: As of September 30, 2021, Arqit's backlog estimates consisted of approximately $130 million in customer contracts.

claims.claim_text: ARQQ's Federated Quantum System (FQS) consortium will enable collaboration between NATO-allied governments for sovereign protection of strategic national assets and interoperability for joint operations, with the first FQS satellites planned for launch on Virgin Orbit's LauncherOne from Newquay in 2023.
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.object_value: FQS satellites 2023 launch via Virgin Orbit
claims.source_quote: Arqit expects that the FQS will enable collaboration between NATO-allied governments, allowing sovereign protection of strategic national assets and interoperability for joint operations. The first FQS satellites are expected to be launched on Virgin Orbit's LauncherOne from Newquay in Cornwall in 2023.

claims.claim_text: ARQQ's current customers include the UK Government, the European Space Agency, BT plc, and Sumitomo Corporation; major customers include named government institutions.
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.source_quote: Arqit's current customers include the UK Government, the European Space Agency, BT plc, and Sumitomo Corporation.

claims.claim_text: Northrup Grumman has contracted to test the use of Arqit's technologies (suggesting a defense-prime channel to U.S. DoD programs).
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.source_quote: Many companies like Verizon, BP, NEOM, Juniper, Dentons, Northrup Grumman and Iridium have contracted to test the use of Arqit's technologies in different use cases.

claims.claim_text: ARQQ is positioned to serve U.S. Department of Defense markets, with senior board members holding prior USAF / DoD acquisition-requirements roles (General Jamieson — USAF ISR & Cyber Effects director; General Wilson — Joint Requirements Oversight Council).
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.source_quote: General Jamieson served as the Director of the United States Air Force's Intelligence Surveillance, Reconnaissance and Cyber Effects enterprise... General Wilson also served on the Joint Requirements Oversight Council setting the acquisition requirements for the Department of Defense.

claims.claim_text: ARQQ's QuantumCloud private-instance product is positioned for government customers at defense Impact Level 5 (IL5), implying U.S. DoD-grade sovereign-cloud deployments.
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.source_quote: Private Instance: QuantumCloud TM can also be sold as a private instance, typically for government customers who want total control over all infrastructure. ... IL5 ...

claims.claim_text: ARQQ has contracted with Qinetiq Space NV for delivery of quantum key distribution satellites by May 2022 and launch readiness review by July 2022, with title passing after launch and in-orbit testing.
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.object_value: Qinetiq QKD satellites May 2022; LRR July 2022
claims.source_quote: On January 27, 2020, Arqit entered into a firm fixed price contract with Qinetiq Space NV or Qinetiq for delivery by Qinetiq of quantum key distribution satellites by May 2022 and for conducting a launch readiness review by July 2022.

claims.claim_text: ARQQ relies on capitalized development costs of $18.2M as of Sept 30, 2021 (vs. $8.8M prior year) — i.e., a substantial portion of expenditure is treated as intangible asset rather than expensed R&D.
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.source_quote: At September 30, 2021, the carrying amount of capitalised development costs were $18,235,034, compared with $8,776,530 at September 30, 2020.

claims.claim_text: ARQQ owns the intellectual property to a novel symmetric-key quantum encryption protocol with universal device applicability (control / patent claim).
claims.subject: ARQQ
claims.source_quote: Arqit has not only invented a ground-breaking new quantum protocol, but it has also found a way to translate the benefits of quantum security to end point devices.
